steps.subject: [InstCombine] Fix select operand simplification with undef (PR47696)

evidence: InstCombine change is about preserving undef and poison semantics in select simplification.
It consults noundef-related guarantees but neither emits attributes nor changes verifier attribute compatibility rules.
features: instcombine, meta:core-llvm, noundef-semantics, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine, path:llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine, term:acomparisonoperanddeclarednoundef
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes InstCombine's select/value-equivalence fold to be an InstCombinerImpl member, allowing it to use the combiner's existing simplification query, dominator tree, and operand-replacement helper. Substantively, it restricts two simplifications of a select's true value so that the comparison operand substituted into the value is proven not to be undef or poison; the added regression test exercises a select whose comparison uses a noundef argument.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::foldSelectValueEquivalence; InstCombinerImpl::foldSelectInstWithICmp; InstCombinerImpl::replaceOperand; select_replacement_sub_noundef
Behavioral change: The fold now requires isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison on CmpRHS before simplifying the true value with CmpLHS replaced by CmpRHS.; The symmetric true-value simplification now requires isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison on CmpLHS before replacing CmpRHS with CmpLHS.; The fold uses the InstCombinerImpl simplification query and replacement helper rather than caller-supplied SimplifyQuery and InstCombiner arguments.; The new test preserves the select when the required non-undef/poison proof is not available; it documents that noundef currently makes the transform safe.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine
Reproducer link: Select/icmp simplification involving undef-or-poison reasoning; A comparison operand declared noundef
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; LLVM IR poison/undef and noundef semantics
Causal explanation: This is directly in InstCombine and explicitly consults noundef-relevant value guarantees, so it is adjacent to the issue's optimizer and attribute-related signal. However, the retrieved implementation neither creates, propagates, nor validates LLVM attributes, and it does not touch Attributor or Verifier. The change restricts a select fold to avoid unsafe undef/poison substitution rather than introducing an attribute/type mismatch, so the evidence for causing the reported "Wrong types for attribute" verifier failure is weak.
Causal confidence: 0.16
Build risk: The declaration, definition, and visible call site of foldSelectValueEquivalence are updated consistently in the retrieved hunks.; A new InstCombine regression test covers the noundef-dependent select case.; The implementation change depends on member-accessible DT and SQ state, so compilation would catch any missing class-state or declaration mismatch.

top_candidates.subject: [Attributor] Fix AANoUndef identification
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Attributor::identifyDefaultAbstractAttributes is extended to create AANoUndef abstract attributes for every return position, formal argument position, and call-site argument position. The accompanying Attributor tests show the resulting expected IR gaining noundef on call operands and a returned argument, and some tests increase the permitted Attributor iteration count from seven to eight.
Changed symbols: Attributor::identifyDefaultAbstractAttributes; AANoUndef; RetPos; ArgPos; CBArgPos
Behavioral change: Attributor now considers noundef inference for all function return positions.; Attributor now considers noundef inference for all formal parameter positions and call-site argument positions.; Manifested optimized IR can gain noundef annotations on call operands and returned arguments, as demonstrated by the changed test expectations.; The internalize test permits one additional Attributor iteration, indicating that the enlarged attribute set can require further convergence.
Assertion or trace link: Attributor; attribute; noundef
Reproducer link: Changed Attributor tests expect noundef on the constant argument to @__kmpc_fork_call, the constant argument to @fn1, the returned argument of @cb1, and the i64 argument to @malloc.; No literal "Wrong types for attribute" or "Broken function found" verifier diagnostic is present in the retrieved hunks.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; Attributor attribute inference; IR attribute manifestation
Causal explanation: This is a direct high-risk match for an Attributor-generated incompatible-attribute failure: the production change substantially broadens the positions for which AANoUndef is created, and the tests confirm that additional noundef attributes reach emitted call-site and function IR. If inference or manifestation permits noundef at an ineligible IR position or type, that can lead to the reported verifier-class failure. The retrieved hunks do not contain the PR48154 reproducer or an actual verifier diagnostic, so the link is strong but not conclusive.
Causal confidence: 0.74
Build risk: Production Attributor attribute-discovery logic changes, with visible output changes in several Attributor tests.; The added AANoUndef requests have no eligibility guard visible in the added hunks; correctness depends on surrounding AANoUndef inference and manifestation handling.; Increasing the test iteration bound from seven to eight signals that analysis convergence behavior changed.

top_candidates.subject: [Value][InstCombine] Fix one-use checks in PHI-of-op -> Op-of-PHI[s] transforms to be one-user checks
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This InstCombine fix changes several PHI-of-operation folding preconditions from one-use to one-user checks. The transformations may now proceed when an instruction is referenced multiple times by the same PHI node, while still rejecting inputs with more than one distinct user. The regression expectation for aggregate PHI reconstruction changes accordingly, preserving separate PHIs and extractvalue operations in the shown test case.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitPHINode; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgInsertValueInstructionIntoPHI; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgGEPIntoPHI; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgOpIntoPHI; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgZextsIntoPHI; Value::hasOneUse; Value::hasOneUser
Behavioral change: PHI-of-op folding now accepts an instruction used more than once when every use is by the same PHI user.; The folds continue to reject operands with multiple distinct users, preserving the no-external-user precondition.; Insertvalue, GEP, generic operation, and zext PHI folds use hasOneUser rather than hasOneUse in the shown checks.; The aggregate PHI regression test's expected optimized form changes for repeated incoming operands.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine; PHI; hasOneUse; hasOneUser
Reproducer link: The covered pattern is a PHI receiving repeated references to the same insertvalue, extractvalue, GEP, zext, or other operation.; The updated aggregate reconstruction test demonstrates changed InstCombine output for repeated PHI incoming values.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; InstCombinePHI.cpp; PHI-of-operation folding

The available evidence therefore does not substantiate a direct causal path to incompatible attribute verification failures.

top_candidates.subject: [Attributor] fix AANoUndef initialization
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This Attributor change corrects AANoUndef initialization by preventing the generic guaranteed-not-undef-or-poison shortcut from applying at IRP_RETURNED positions. The accompanying tests update expected Attributor output to remove noundef from affected call returns and call-site arguments, including returned-value SCC cases, while retaining other inferred pointer attributes such as nonnull, alignment, dereferenceable, noalias, and nocapture where applicable.
Changed symbols: AANoUndefImpl; AANoUndef; IRPosition::IRP_RETURNED; isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison; Attributor
Behavioral change: AANoUndefImpl no longer initializes returned-value positions as noundef merely because the underlying value is guaranteed not to be undef or poison.; The special-case exclusion is restricted to IRPosition::IRP_RETURNED; other position kinds retain the prior guaranteed-not-undef-or-poison initialization path.; Expected Attributor output removes inferred noundef in call-return, propagated call-argument, and returned-value SCC scenarios shown by the updated tests.
Assertion or trace link: Attributor; AANoUndef; noundef; attribute
Reproducer link: memory_locations.ll now expects @unknown_ptr and @argmem_only call results/arguments without noundef.; dereferenceable-1.ll now expects returned and argument pointer values to retain nonnull/alignment/dereferenceable attributes but not noundef.; returned.ll removes noundef from values propagated through returned-value SCC calls.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; AttributorAttributes.cpp; returned-value and call-site attribute propagation
Causal explanation: The candidate directly repairs inference and propagation of an IR attribute in Attributor, matching the issue's concern that Attributor optimization yields verifier-invalid or incompatible attributes. In particular, excluding IRP_RETURNED prevents a blanket noundef conclusion for return positions and the tests demonstrate that this conclusion had propagated to call results and arguments. The retrieved evidence does not show a verifier failure or establish that noundef is the exact attribute named in the issue's "Wrong types for attribute" diagnostic, but it is a close and concrete attribute-inference match.
Causal confidence: 0.77
Build risk: The implementation change is narrowly scoped to AANoUndef initialization; no build-system changes are shown.; Multiple Attributor regression tests change expected emitted attributes, signaling potentially broad output differences in optimized IR.; Test coverage spans memory-location inference, heap-to-stack-related output, dereferenceability, noalias, and returned-value propagation.

steps.subject: [Attributor] fix AANoUndef initialization

evidence: Directly fixes erroneous AANoUndef initialization for returned-value positions and removes emitted noundef from affected IR.
It strongly localizes the relevant bad inference area, but its corrective direction makes it less likely to be the first bad boundary than the original noundef introduction.
features: attribute-manifestation, attributor, meta:core-llvm, noundef-inference, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/IPO, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes Attributor's AANoUndef initialization so that the generic `isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison` proof is not used for returned-value positions. The accompanying Attributor test updates consistently remove inferred `noundef` from several return values and call arguments, including unknown-pointer and heap-allocation cases.
Changed symbols: AANoUndefImpl; AANoUndef; AANoUndefImpl::initialize; IRPosition::IRP_RETURNED; callerC1; test1; f7_2; return_noalias_looks_like_capture
Behavioral change: AANoUndef inference no longer initializes a returned-value position as known non-undef/non-poison solely from `isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison`.; Attributor consequently stops emitting some `noundef` attributes on returned values and at call sites that receive or forward those values.; The updated checks unify prior pipeline-specific expectations around the reduced `noundef` inference.
Assertion or trace link: Attributor; attribute; noundef; Wrong types for attribute
Reproducer link: The changed tests cover calls returning unknown pointers, malloc-derived pointers, dereferenceable pointers, and pointer-return SCCs where prior expected output contained `noundef`.; In `callerC1`, the expected return from `@unknown_ptr` and argument passed to `@argmem_only` lose `noundef`.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; AANoUndef attribute inference; LLVM IR attribute emission
Causal explanation: This is a direct Attributor attribute-inference correction in the area implicated by the issue. An incorrectly inferred `noundef` on a returned value can be propagated to declarations, calls, or returns and may lead to verifier-rejected attribute placement or type incompatibility. The retrieved hunk does not show a verifier diagnostic or the PR reproducer itself, but it explicitly constrains the inference that generated the removed attributes.
Causal confidence: 0.78
Build risk: Production Attributor implementation change accompanied by multiple regression-test expectation updates.; The change alters emitted IR attributes, which can expose pipeline-specific test differences.; No retrieved hunk directly modifies Verifier.cpp or adds an explicit verifier-failure regression.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes Attributor's AANoUndef initialization so that the generic `isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison` proof is not used for returned-value positions. The accompanying Attributor test updates consistently remove inferred `noundef` from several return values and call arguments, including unknown-pointer and heap-allocation cases.
Changed symbols: AANoUndefImpl; AANoUndef; AANoUndefImpl::initialize; IRPosition::IRP_RETURNED; callerC1; test1; f7_2; return_noalias_looks_like_capture
Behavioral change: AANoUndef inference no longer initializes a returned-value position as known non-undef/non-poison solely from `isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison`.; Attributor consequently stops emitting some `noundef` attributes on returned values and at call sites that receive or forward those values.; The updated checks unify prior pipeline-specific expectations around the reduced `noundef` inference.
Assertion or trace link: Attributor; attribute; noundef; Wrong types for attribute
Reproducer link: The changed tests cover calls returning unknown pointers, malloc-derived pointers, dereferenceable pointers, and pointer-return SCCs where prior expected output contained `noundef`.; In `callerC1`, the expected return from `@unknown_ptr` and argument passed to `@argmem_only` lose `noundef`.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; AANoUndef attribute inference; LLVM IR attribute emission
Causal explanation: This is a direct Attributor attribute-inference correction in the area implicated by the issue. An incorrectly inferred `noundef` on a returned value can be propagated to declarations, calls, or returns and may lead to verifier-rejected attribute placement or type incompatibility. The retrieved hunk does not show a verifier diagnostic or the PR reproducer itself, but it explicitly constrains the inference that generated the removed attributes.
Causal confidence: 0.78
Build risk: Production Attributor implementation change accompanied by multiple regression-test expectation updates.; The change alters emitted IR attributes, which can expose pipeline-specific test differences.; No retrieved hunk directly modifies Verifier.cpp or adds an explicit verifier-failure regression.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This Attributor fix removes a nonnull inference shortcut in AANonNullFloating that concluded nonnull from an AADereferenceable result when null is undefined. The stated purpose is to avoid using cyclic arguments for nonnull. The test updates reduce Attributor iteration limits in several existing tests, consistent with changed convergence or dependency behavior after removing that cyclic dependency path.
Changed symbols: AANonNullFloating; AANonNullFloating::updateImpl; AADereferenceable
Behavioral change: AANonNullFloating no longer preserves its current state solely because the corresponding AADereferenceable analysis reports assumed dereferenceable bytes when null is undefined.; Nonnull inference no longer depends on that dereferenceability-to-nonnull shortcut, eliminating the shown potential cyclic analysis relationship.; Several Attributor test invocations lower their maximum analysis iterations, from three to one or from two to one/two depending on the test.
Assertion or trace link: Attributor; nonnull attribute inference; cyclic arguments; No verifier assertion or exact "Wrong types for attribute" diagnostic is present in the retrieved evidence.
Reproducer link: The commit subject identifies cyclic arguments as the nonnull-analysis trigger.; The selected Attributor and ArgumentPromotion tests adjust maximum iteration counts after the dependency is removed.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; llvm/lib/Transforms/IPO/AttributorAttributes.cpp; No InstCombine or Verifier implementation is changed in the candidate hunks.
Causal explanation: The change is directly in Attributor's nonnull inference and removes a route that can feed inferred attributes through cyclic argument analysis. Since the issue involves Attributor-generated incompatible attributes, cyclic or over-aggressive nonnull deduction is plausibly related. However, the shown change removes an inference path rather than adding one, and neither the selected implementation hunk nor tests demonstrate a verifier-invalid attribute; it is therefore better supported as a possible mitigation than as a demonstrated source of the crash.
Causal confidence: 0.71
Build risk: Small implementation change, but it alters dependencies between AANonNull and AADereferenceable analyses.; No build-system changes are shown.; Test command iteration limits changed, signaling altered fixpoint/convergence behavior; selected tests do not explicitly invoke or check the verifier.

top_candidates.subject: [Attributor][FIX] Handle function pointers properly in AANonNull
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This Attributor change makes AANonNull conservative for GlobalValue-associated values, including function values, by immediately reaching a pessimistic fixpoint instead of following uses. It also changes AANonNullReturned to use AANonNull as its returned-value base and supplies a nonnull-specific string representation. The accompanying tests remove previously inferred nonnull annotations from bitcast function pointers passed through OpenMP callbacks and other callback/function-pointer paths.
Changed symbols: AANonNullImpl; AANonNullReturned; AAReturnedFromReturnedValues; AANonNullImpl::getAsStr
Behavioral change: AANonNullImpl now pessimistically stops nonnull inference when its associated value is a GlobalValue, rather than traversing uses in the MBEC analysis.; Returned-value nonnull analysis changes its base composition from AANonNullImpl to AANonNull.; Attributor no longer manifests inferred nonnull on several global function-pointer values and bitcast function-pointer callback operands, as reflected by updated checks.
Assertion or trace link: Attributor; nonnull attribute inference; No verifier assertion or exact "Wrong types for attribute" diagnostic is present in the retrieved evidence.
Reproducer link: Function values are bitcast to pointer types and returned or passed as callback arguments.; The updated OpenMP and callback checks specifically remove nonnull from bitcast function-pointer operands.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; llvm/lib/Transforms/IPO/AttributorAttributes.cpp; No InstCombine or Verifier implementation is changed in the retrieved hunks.
Causal explanation: The issue concerns verifier-incompatible attributes produced during Attributor/InstCombine optimization. This commit directly changes Attributor's placement and inference of the type-sensitive nonnull attribute on function-pointer/global-value paths, and its tests demonstrate that previously emitted nonnull annotations are removed. That is a strong mechanism for avoiding an invalid attribute manifestation, although the retrieved hunks do not show the reported verifier diagnostic or an InstCombine interaction.
Causal confidence: 0.84
Build risk: Implementation-only Attributor attribute-analysis change; no build-system changes are shown.; Regression expectations were updated across Attributor nonnull, callbacks, liveness, OpenMP constant propagation, and miscellaneous tests.; Selected tests validate emitted IR but do not explicitly show a verifier-failure check.

Summary: This InstCombine commit corrects several PHI-of-operation folding guards by replacing `hasOneUse()` with `hasOneUser()`. The transforms now permit an incoming instruction to be referenced multiple times by the same PHI while still rejecting values used by multiple distinct users; the updated aggregate reconstruction test reflects the resulting non-folded or differently structured PHIs.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitPHINode; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgInsertValueInstructionIntoPHI; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgGEPIntoPHI; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgOpIntoPHI; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgZextsIntoPHI; Value::hasOneUser; Value::hasOneUse
Behavioral change: PHI-of-op-to-op-of-PHI transformations treat repeated incoming-edge references from one PHI as a single user rather than multiple uses.; The affected insertvalue, GEP, generic operation, and zext folds become eligible when an instruction's only user is the PHI, even if that PHI uses it on more than one incoming edge.; Values with an external user remain ineligible for these folds because the new guard still requires exactly one distinct user.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit introduces Attributor deduction and manifestation support for the noundef attribute. It registers AANoUndef analysis for pointer-valued function returns, formal arguments, and call-site arguments, then implements noundef state initialization and propagation through casts, GEPs, generic value traversal, returned values, and call-site/argument relationships. Updated tests expect noundef to be added to pointer arguments and call operands.
Changed symbols: Attributor::identifyDefaultAbstractAttributes; AANoUndefImpl; AANoUndefFloating; AANoUndefReturned; AANoUndefArgument; AANoUndefCallSiteArgument; AANoUndefImpl::initialize; AANoUndefImpl::followUseInMBEC
Behavioral change: Attributor creates AANoUndef attributes for pointer return positions, pointer formal-argument positions, and pointer call-site-argument positions.; The new analysis treats undef as pessimistic, freeze values and values guaranteed not undef-or-poison as optimistic, and otherwise uses the existing AANoUndef initialization path.; Noundef information propagates through tracked casts and GEPs and through generic value, returned-value, and call-site/argument analyses.; Attributor output gains noundef on pointer call operands and pointer formal arguments in the updated tests.

Reproducer link: Pointer arguments and call operands receive newly inferred noundef annotations.; The visible tests expect noundef on an inalloca pointer argument and on pointer arguments passed by calls.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; llvm/lib/Transforms/IPO/Attributor.cpp; llvm/lib/Transforms/IPO/AttributorAttributes.cpp; No InstCombine or Verifier implementation is changed in the retrieved hunks.

The code explicitly expands analysis to pointer returns, arguments, and call-site arguments, matching the issue's Attributor/attribute-propagation focus. Summary: Reverts part of InstCombine's equality-conditioned select simplification. The change removes the path in foldSelectValueEquivalence that used SimplifyWithOpReplaced to rewrite a select arm under the assumption that compared operands are interchangeable, and changes the helper to return a Value so the caller performs whole-select use replacement. Tests are adjusted to leave vector/undef cases unsimplified and to expect a less-aggressive remainder/select form.
Changed symbols: foldSelectValueEquivalence; InstCombinerImpl::foldSelectInstWithICmp; replaceInstUsesWith; select_xor_icmp_vec_bad_2; biggest_divisor
Behavioral change: Removes simplification of the true select operand by substituting one equality-compare operand for the other through SimplifyWithOpReplaced.; Restores a model where foldSelectValueEquivalence returns a replacement Value and foldSelectInstWithICmp replaces all uses of the original select.; Explicitly avoids the vector compare case containing undef because identity-constant matching does not safely handle it.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine
Reproducer link: The added/renamed vector test contains an equality compare against a vector with an undef lane and verifies that the select remains unsimplified.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; InstCombineSelect
Causal explanation: This is an InstCombine correctness rollback involving undef-sensitive select rewriting, so it is plausibly relevant to optimizer-produced invalid IR in a broad sense. However, the retrieved hunks neither modify Attributor nor manipulate function/call attributes, and contain no verifier rule or diagnostic related to "Wrong types for attribute" or "Broken function found". The evidence therefore supports only an indirect connection to the reported issue.
Causal confidence: 0.15
Build risk: Changes foldSelectValueEquivalence's return type and removes its InstCombiner parameter, requiring all declarations and callers to agree.; Regression expectations change in InstCombine select and remainder tests.; No verifier or Attributor test coverage is visible in the retrieved hunks.

top_candidates.subject: [Attributor] Fix AANoUndef identification
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Attributor::identifyDefaultAbstractAttributes is changed to create AANoUndef abstract attributes for every function return position, every function argument position, and every call-site argument position. This expands the positions at which Attributor can infer and manifest noundef, with test expectations updated to show noundef on integer constants, pointer arguments, and a returned callback parameter.
Changed symbols: Attributor::identifyDefaultAbstractAttributes; AANoUndef; RetPos; ArgPos; CBArgPos
Behavioral change: Attributor now initializes noundef analysis for function return positions.; Attributor now initializes noundef analysis for function argument positions.; Attributor now initializes noundef analysis for call-site argument positions.; Attributor output can consequently gain manifested noundef attributes at additional return, parameter, and call-argument locations.
Assertion or trace link: Wrong types for attribute; Broken function found; attribute; Attributor
Reproducer link: The updated tests explicitly expect new noundef annotations on an i32 call argument, a pointer call argument, and a callback parameter.; The internalize test raises -attributor-max-iterations from 7 to 8, indicating the added AANoUndef positions affect Attributor's convergence/output.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; AANoUndef; IR attribute inference and manifestation
Causal explanation: This is a strong causal candidate because it directly expands Attributor's attribute inference and propagation to returns, formal arguments, and call-site arguments. The issue concerns verifier-rejected IR with incompatible attributes after Attributor/InstCombine processing. The visible evidence does not show a verifier rule, a type-compatibility guard, or the exact failing IR, so it cannot establish that noundef is the incompatible attribute; nevertheless, this commit materially increases the set of IR locations receiving an attribute implicated by the issue.
Causal confidence: 0.68
Build risk: Changes optimizer-produced IR attributes rather than only tests.; Requires additional Attributor iteration in the internalize test configuration.; Multiple Attributor regression tests change expected IR to include noundef, increasing sensitivity to attribute-placement and call-site consistency.

top_candidates.subject: Revert "[InstCombine] Canonicalize SPF_ABS to abs intrinc"
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Reverts InstCombine canonicalization of select-based absolute-value patterns into llvm.abs intrinsics. canonicalizeAbsNabs is restored to canonicalize equivalent select/compare/negation shapes into a standard select form, including compare operand/predicate normalization, construction or reuse of a negation, select-arm swapping, and corresponding profile-metadata swapping. Tests now expect compare/sub/select IR rather than llvm.abs calls.
Changed symbols: canonicalizeAbsNabs; SelectInst::swapValues; SelectInst::swapProfMetadata; abs_nabs_x01; abs_of_min_of_not; abs_abs_x01; cttz_abs_multiuse
Behavioral change: Stops replacing matched select-based ABS/NABS expressions with llvm.abs intrinsics.; Canonicalizes the comparison to an icmp slt against integer zero where needed.; Canonicalizes the negated select operand to sub 0, LHS when profitability/use-count conditions permit.; Swaps select values and profile metadata together when canonical operand order requires it.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine
Reproducer link: The modified tests cover scalar and vector ABS/NABS select forms, metadata preservation, nested min/abs patterns, and multi-use results.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; InstCombineSelect
Causal explanation: The candidate is in the affected optimizer subsystem and changes IR construction substantially, including metadata-preserving select rewrites. Nevertheless, the retrieved evidence is limited to arithmetic/select canonicalization and llvm.abs intrinsic formation; it does not show Attributor inference, attribute propagation, call-site rewriting, verifier changes, or an incompatible-attribute diagnostic. It is consequently a weak candidate for an Attributor/verifier attribute crash.
Causal confidence: 0.12
Build risk: Restores mutation of compare predicates and operands, select operands, and profile metadata; correctness depends on preserving the matched select semantics.; Uses assertions concerning negation shape and RHS use counts, so unusual matched forms are guarded by internal invariants.; Multiple InstCombine output tests are updated from llvm.abs calls to compare/sub/select sequences.; No Attributor or verifier regression test is visible.

Summary: This InstCombine change replaces several VectorType::getNumElements uses with FixedVectorType::getNumElements or casts to FixedVectorType in bitcast, shuffle-vector, compare, pointer-to-integer, and demanded-elements transforms. The practical invariant is narrowed from generic vector types to fixed-width vectors at these element-count-dependent transformation sites.

top_candidates.subject: Revert "[InstCombine] Take 2: Perform trivial PHI CSE"
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert disables InstCombine's trivial PHI common-subexpression elimination. It removes the visitPHINode loop that searched earlier PHIs in the same block for an identical definition and replaced the current PHI's uses with that earlier PHI, removes the corresponding statistic, and restores tests that retain separate equivalent pointer PHIs after InstCombine.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitPHINode; NumPHICSEs
Behavioral change: InstCombine no longer scans preceding PHIs in a basic block for isIdenticalToWhenDefined() matches.; Equivalent PHIs are no longer replaced through replaceInstUsesWith() by this InstCombine PHI-CSE logic.; The reverted tests preserve distinct pointer PHIs after InstCombine; one test separately shows that a later InstCombine-plus-GVN pipeline can still eliminate equivalent pointer computations.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine
Reproducer link: identical pointer PHIs feeding loads and stores in the same basic block
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine
Causal explanation: The commit changes use replacement and PHI deduplication in InstCombine, which could alter the IR seen by later optimization passes. The retrieved tests include a call checked with a nonnull argument, but the reverted implementation itself only compares identical PHIs and replaces value uses; it does not modify attributes, invoke Attributor, or alter verifier rules. No evidence connects this PHI-CSE revert to "Wrong types for attribute" or "Broken function found", making it a weak candidate for the stated issue.
Causal confidence: 0.12
Build risk: The revert removes both the PHI-CSE implementation and its statistic use.; InstCombine and InstCombine-plus-GVN FileCheck expectations are updated for the restored behavior.; No retrieved test exercises Attributor, verifier diagnostics, or incompatible function/call-site attributes.

steps.subject: [Attributor] Fix AANoUndef identification

evidence: Directly expands Attributor AANoUndef creation and manifestation to return positions, formal arguments, and call-site arguments.
This newly attaches noundef across many more typed IR positions, directly matching verifier evidence about incompatible attribute types after Attributor optimization.
features: attribute-manifestation, attributor, callsite-attributes, meta:core-llvm, noundef, parameter-attributes
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This Attributor change expands default AANoUndef discovery so that the pass creates noundef abstract attributes for every function return position, every formal argument position, and every call-site argument position. The accompanying Attributor tests change expected IR to include newly manifested noundef attributes on scalar and pointer call operands and on a returned argument.
Changed symbols: Attributor::identifyDefaultAbstractAttributes; AANoUndef; getOrCreateAAFor
Behavioral change: Creates AANoUndef for each RetPos, allowing return values to be inferred and manifested as noundef.; Creates AANoUndef for each ArgPos, allowing function parameters to be inferred and manifested as noundef.; Creates AANoUndef for each CBArgPos, allowing call-site operands to be inferred and manifested as noundef.; Changes Attributor-produced IR by adding noundef to call operands, as shown for constant integer arguments, OpenMP runtime call operands, malloc size operands, and a returned callback parameter.
Assertion or trace link: Attributor; attribute; noundef
Reproducer link: Attributor test expectations now require noundef on call-site arguments such as i32 3, i64 42, and i64 10.; Attributor test expectations now require noundef on pointer call operands and on a returned i32 function parameter.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; LLVM IR function and call-site attribute propagation
Causal explanation: This is a direct high-risk match for an Attributor verifier failure involving incompatible attributes: it broadens the set of return, formal-argument, and call-site positions at which Attributor may manifest noundef. If any newly covered position has a type or placement for which the manifested attribute is invalid, the verifier could report an attribute-type incompatibility. The retrieved hunks do not themselves show a verifier diagnostic or an invalid type case, but they provide direct evidence of broad new attribute propagation in the implicated pass.
Causal confidence: 0.84
Build risk: Multiple Attributor regression expectations change because generated IR gains noundef attributes.; The internalize test raises attributor-max-iterations from 7 to 8, signaling that the added abstract attributes affect convergence/worklist behavior.; The change touches return, declaration-argument, and call-site-argument attribution paths, increasing output sensitivity across Attributor pipelines.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit reverts InstCombine's trivial PHI common-subexpression elimination. It removes the visitPHINode() logic that replaced an identical PHI with an earlier PHI in the same block, removes its statistic, and updates InstCombine tests to expect separate PHIs to remain after the pass.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitPHINode; NumPHICSEs; test_gep_and_bitcast_same_bb; test_gep_and_bitcast_same_bb_and_extra_use; phi-aware-aggregate-reconstruction
Behavioral change: InstCombine no longer scans earlier PHIs in a block for an identical PHI and replaces the current PHI's uses with that earlier PHI.; Identical pointer and aggregate PHIs can remain distinct after InstCombine, as reflected in updated test expectations.; The PHI-CSE statistic is removed because the reverted optimization no longer executes.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine; No retrieved hunk contains "Wrong types for attribute", "Broken function found", or another verifier diagnostic.
Reproducer link: The affected tests exercise equivalent GEP/bitcast-derived pointer PHIs and aggregate PHIs.; One visible test context includes a call with a nonnull pointer argument, but the reverted implementation itself only compares and replaces identical PHI nodes.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; InstCombinePHI
Causal explanation: The commit directly changes InstCombine IR rewriting, which gives it a broad optimizer-risk connection to the issue. But the shown rewrite is limited to equivalent PHI nodes and does not create, transfer, or validate function or call-site attributes. The visible tests concern PHI identity and pointer/aggregate reconstruction, not incompatible attribute types, so the evidence-backed connection to the reported Attributor/verifier failure is weak.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Production InstCombine behavior is removed, with test expectations updated for the less-canonical PHI form.; The revert may alter optimization output and downstream pass interactions, particularly where duplicate PHIs previously shared uses.; No build breakage or verifier failure is shown in the retrieved hunks.

Summary: This commit reverts the InstCombine PHI-of-extractvalue-to-extractvalue-of-PHI transform. It removes the transform implementation, its declaration and statistic, and the dispatch from foldPHIArgOpIntoPHI, restoring the prior behavior in which matching extractvalue incoming values remain represented through PHIs rather than synthesizing aggregate PHIs followed by extractvalue instructions.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgExtractValueInstructionIntoPHI; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgOpIntoPHI; InstCombinerImpl::foldPHIArgInsertValueInstructionIntoPHI; InstCombineInternal.h; NumPHIsOfExtractValues
Behavioral change: Disables folding a PHI whose incoming values are matching single-use ExtractValueInst instructions into an aggregate-typed PHI plus one ExtractValueInst.; Removes creation of PHINode instances for aggregate operands and the corresponding ExtractValueInst replacement.; Restores InstCombine test expectations to retain a merged aggregate PHI form rather than the reconstructed aggregate-PHI/extractvalue form.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine
Reproducer link: The affected transform operates on PHIs of extractvalue instructions over aggregate values.; No retrieved hunk contains a verifier failure, "Wrong types for attribute", "Broken function found", or an Attributor reproducer.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine; InstCombine PHI folding
Causal explanation: The commit is directly in InstCombine and removes a transformation whose subject explicitly notes that invokes are problematic, so it could eliminate malformed or otherwise problematic IR produced by that fold. However, the retrieved implementation only rewrites aggregate PHIs and extractvalue instructions; it neither reads nor writes function, call-site, or parameter attributes, and it does not touch Attributor or the verifier. The evidence therefore supports only an indirect InstCombine-side connection to the reported optimizer/verifier failure.
Causal confidence: 0.20
Build risk: Implementation, declaration, dispatch, statistic, and InstCombine regression-test expectations are updated consistently.; The visible test change covers aggregate-PHI output shape, not verifier validation or attribute compatibility.; No Attributor or Verifier test coverage is present in the retrieved hunks.

top_candidates.subject: [Attributor] Do not manifest noundef for dead positions
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit prevents Attributor's AANoUndef implementation from manifesting noundef on positions that Attributor considers dead. The new manifest override returns unchanged for dead IR positions because their associated values can be replaced with undef; accompanying Attributor tests update expected IR to remove noundef from dead undef-valued arguments while retaining other inferred attributes where applicable.
Changed symbols: AANoUndefImpl::manifest; AANoUndef::manifest; Attributor::isAssumedDead; returned_dead; argument_dead_callback_callee; callback_caller; pthread_create
Behavioral change: AANoUndefImpl now checks whether its IR position is assumed dead before manifesting an inferred noundef attribute.; For a dead position, noundef is not added and manifest returns ChangeStatus::UNCHANGED.; For a live position, manifesting delegates to the existing AANoUndef::manifest behavior.; Regression expectations remove noundef from call arguments transformed to undef or otherwise associated with dead positions, including callback and interprocedural constant-propagation cases.
Assertion or trace link: Attributor; noundef; undef; verifier; incompatible attributes
Reproducer link: The new returned_dead test expects a dead return value to become undef without adding noundef to the return.; The callback_caller test expects the dead callback argument to become undef without noundef in the IS__TUNIT__ result.; The pthread and IPConstantProp expectation updates remove noundef specifically from arguments that are represented as undef or determined dead.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; AttributorAttributes; Attributor IPConstantProp; module Attributor
Causal explanation: This is a direct match for the issue's high-risk subsystem and attribute-inference mechanism. The added guard explicitly identifies the hazardous sequence: Attributor may replace values at dead positions with undef, so manifesting noundef there is inappropriate. Preventing that attribute attachment plausibly avoids invalid or verifier-rejected IR produced after Attributor optimization. The retrieved evidence does not include the exact PR48154 diagnostic text, so the link is strong but not proven to be the exact reported reproducer.
Causal confidence: 0.86
Build risk: The change is narrowly scoped to AANoUndefImpl manifestation and preserves existing behavior for non-dead positions.; Multiple Attributor regression suites were updated, including noundef, callbacks, IPConstantProp, argument promotion, and a misc_crash test.; The new behavior relies on Attributor liveness classification through isAssumedDead; an incorrect liveness result could suppress valid noundef inference, but the visible tests cover several dead-position forms.

Summary: The change adds AANoUndefImpl::manifest, which suppresses Attributor's manifesting of the noundef attribute when the associated IR position is assumed dead. The accompanying Attributor tests update expected IR so that values rewritten to undef at dead call-site or argument positions no longer retain noundef.

top_candidates.subject: [Attributor] Do not manifest noundef for dead positions
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The change adds AANoUndefImpl::manifest, which suppresses Attributor's manifesting of the noundef attribute when the associated IR position is assumed dead. The accompanying Attributor tests update expected IR so that values rewritten to undef at dead call-site or argument positions no longer retain noundef.
Changed symbols: AANoUndefImpl::manifest; AANoUndef::manifest; Attributor::isAssumedDead; returned_dead; callback_caller
Behavioral change: Before delegating to AANoUndef::manifest, AANoUndefImpl now queries whether its IRPosition is assumed dead.; For an assumed-dead position, the attribute is left unchanged rather than adding noundef.; This prevents noundef from being attached to values that Attributor's dead-position handling replaces with undef.; Regression expectations remove noundef from dead undef call operands and from inferred attributes on dead argument positions.
Assertion or trace link: noundef; dead positions; undef; Attributor
Reproducer link: The pthread_create test changes expected dead call arguments from noundef undef to undef without noundef.; The noundef test adds a dead returned value rewritten to undef and a callback argument whose TUnit Attributor result is undef without noundef.; Existing Attributor tests for constant propagation, argument promotion, and crash cases are updated to omit noundef on inferred dead positions.
Pass or subsystem link: Attributor; IR attribute manifestation; module/TUnit and CGSCC Attributor pipelines
Causal explanation: This is a direct match for the issue's Attributor-and-attribute risk area. The patch explicitly fixes an invalid combination in which Attributor inferred noundef while another dead-position transformation replaced the corresponding value with undef. That can create malformed or semantically contradictory optimized IR and plausibly lead to verifier failures after optimization. The retrieved evidence does not prove that the exact verifier wording "Wrong types for attribute" is emitted by this path, but it strongly establishes a causal mechanism involving Attributor attribute propagation and invalid post-transform IR.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Value::dropDroppableUse is adjusted while rewriting llvm.assume operand-bundle uses: after replacing a non-condition bundle operand with an undef value and retagging its bundle as "ignore", the bundle-tag lookup now uses the owning assume instruction's LLVMContext rather than the context obtained from the Value whose use is being dropped. A new SROA regression test verifies that an assume nonnull bundle tied to a removed alloca-derived pointer becomes an ignore bundle containing typed undef.
Changed symbols: Value::dropDroppableUse; llvm.assume; CallInst::BundleOpInfo; getOrInsertBundleTag; _ZN2bg2baIiEC2ES_ SROA regression test
Behavioral change: For a droppable non-condition llvm.assume operand-bundle use, the replacement still changes the operand to typed undef and retags the bundle as "ignore".; The "ignore" bundle tag is now interned through Assume->getContext() rather than Value::getContext().; The new SROA test establishes expected preservation of the assume call while changing a "nonnull" pointer bundle to "ignore" with a %struct.bi* undef operand.
Assertion or trace link: The candidate touches llvm.assume operand bundles, which are IR semantic metadata-like operands, but it contains no "Wrong types for attribute", "Broken function found", verifier assertion, InstCombine trace, or Attributor trace.
Reproducer link: The regression reproduces SROA dropping an alloca-derived pointer use from a "nonnull" assume bundle and retagging that bundle to "ignore".; It does not reproduce the reported InstCombine/Attributor incompatible-attribute failure.
Pass or subsystem link: SROA; LLVM IR Value use rewriting; llvm.assume operand bundles

+//===-- MachineFunctionSplitter.cpp - Split machine functions //-----------===//
+//

+// See https://llvm.org/LICENSE.txt for license information.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+//
+// \file
+// Uses profile information to split out cold blocks.
+//
+// This pass splits out cold machine basic blocks from the parent function. This
+// implementation leverages the basic block section framework. Blocks marked
+// cold by this pass are grouped together in a separate section prefixed with
+// ".text.unlikely.*". The linker can then group these together as a cold
+// section. The split part of the function is a contiguous region identified by
+// the symbol "foo.cold". Grouping all cold blocks across functions together
+// decreases fragmentation and improves icache and itlb utilization. Note that
+// the overall changes to the binary size are negligible; only a small number of
+// additional jump instructions may be introduced.
+//
+// For the original RFC of this pass please see
+// https://groups.google.com/d/msg/llvm-dev/RUegaMg-iqc/wFAVxa6fCgAJ
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+
+#include "llvm/ADT/Statistic.h"
+#include "llvm/Analysis/ProfileSummaryInfo.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/BasicBlockSectionUtils.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineBasicBlock.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineBlockFrequencyInfo.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineFunction.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineFunctionPass.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineModuleInfo.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/Passes.h"
+#include "llvm/IR/Function.h"
+#include "llvm/IR/Module.h"
+#include "llvm/InitializePasses.h"
+#include "llvm/Support/CommandLine.h"
+
+using namespace llvm;
+
+static cl::opt<unsigned>
+    PercentileCutoff("mfs-psi-cutoff",
+                     cl::desc("Percentile profile summary cutoff used to "
+                              "determine cold blocks. Unused if set to zero."),
+                     cl::init(0), cl::Hidden);
+
+static cl::opt<unsigned> ColdCountThreshold(
+    "mfs-count-threshold",
+    cl::desc(
+        "Minimum number of times a block must be executed to be retained."),
+    cl::init(1), cl::Hidden);
+
+namespace {
+
+class MachineFunctionSplitter : public MachineFunctionPass {
+public:
+  static char ID;
+  MachineFunctionSplitter() : MachineFunctionPass(ID) {
+    initializeMachineFunctionSplitterPass(*PassRegistry::getPassRegistry());
+  }
+
+  StringRef getPassName() const override {
+    return "Machine Function Splitter Transformation";
+  }
+
+  void getAnalysisUsage(AnalysisUsage &AU) const override;
+

+  }
+  return (*Count < ColdCountThreshold);

+//===-- MachineFunctionSplitter.cpp - Split machine functions //-----------===//
+//
+// Part of the LLVM Project, under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions.
+// See https://llvm.org/LICENSE.txt for license information.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+//
+// \file
+// Uses profile information to split out cold blocks.
+//
+// This pass splits out cold machine basic blocks from the parent function. This
+// implementation leverages the basic block section framework. Blocks marked
+// cold by this pass are grouped together in a separate section prefixed with
+// ".text.unlikely.*". The linker can then group these together as a cold
+// section. The split part of the function is a contiguous region identified by
+// the symbol "foo.cold". Grouping all cold blocks across functions together
+// decreases fragmentation and improves icache and itlb utilization. Note that
+// the overall changes to the binary size are negligible; only a small number of
+// additional jump instructions may be introduced.
+//
+// For the original RFC of this pass please see
+// https://groups.google.com/d/msg/llvm-dev/RUegaMg-iqc/wFAVxa6fCgAJ
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+
+#include "llvm/ADT/Statistic.h"
+#include "llvm/Analysis/ProfileSummaryInfo.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/BasicBlockSectionUtils.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineBasicBlock.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineBlockFrequencyInfo.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineFunction.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineFunctionPass.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineModuleInfo.h"
+#include "llvm/CodeGen/Passes.h"
+#include "llvm/IR/Function.h"
+#include "llvm/IR/Module.h"
+#include "llvm/InitializePasses.h"
+#include "llvm/Support/CommandLine.h"
+
+using namespace llvm;
+
+static cl::opt<unsigned>
+    PercentileCutoff("mfs-psi-cutoff",
+                     cl::desc("Percentile profile summary cutoff used to "
+                              "determine cold blocks. Unused if set to zero."),
+                     cl::init(0), cl::Hidden);
+
+static cl::opt<unsigned> ColdCountThreshold(
+    "mfs-count-threshold",
+    cl::desc(
+        "Minimum number of times a block must be executed to be retained."),
+    cl::init(1), cl::Hidden);
+
+namespace {
+
+class MachineFunctionSplitter : public MachineFunctionPass {
+public:
+  static char ID;
+  MachineFunctionSplitter() : MachineFunctionPass(ID) {
+    initializeMachineFunctionSplitterPass(*PassRegistry::getPassRegistry());
+  }
+
+  StringRef getPassName() const override {
+    return "Machine Function Splitter Transformation";
+  }
+
+  void getAnalysisUsage(AnalysisUsage &AU) const override;
+
+  bool runOnMachineFunction(MachineFunction &F) override;
+};
+} // end anonymous namespace
+
+static bool isColdBlock(MachineBasicBlock &MBB,
+                        const MachineBlockFrequencyInfo *MBFI,
+                        ProfileSummaryInfo *PSI) {
+  Optional<uint64_t> Count = MBFI->getBlockProfileCount(&MBB);
+  if (!Count.hasValue())
+    return true;
+
+  if (PercentileCutoff > 0) {
+    return PSI->isColdCountNthPercentile(PercentileCutoff, *Count);
+  }
+  return (*Count < ColdCountThreshold);
+}
+

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This reland adds AArch64 support for the Clang arm_sve_vector_bits attribute. The retrieved code introduces ABI coercion of fixed-length SVE vector types to corresponding scalable LLVM vector ABI types and adds Itanium mangling for fixed-length SVE vector and predicate types; new CodeGen tests verify casts, globals, and mangled names for several SVE vector widths.
Changed symbols: AArch64ABIInfo::coerceIllegalVector; CXXNameMangler::mangleAArch64FixedSveVectorType; CXXNameMangler::mangleAArch64FixedSveVectorType(const DependentVectorType *)
Behavioral change: Fixed-length SVE data and predicate vector types are coerced to specific scalable LLVM vector types for AArch64 ABI argument handling.; Non-SVE illegal vector coercion retains size-based scalar, fixed-vector, or indirect ABI handling.; Itanium mangling now encodes fixed-length SVE types using the __SVE_VLS pseudo-template form with the selected vector length.; Tests establish emitted LLVM IR containing bitcasts between fixed and scalable vector representations for arm_sve_vector_bits types.
Assertion or trace link: attribute; arm_sve_vector_bits
Reproducer link: The new tests exercise Clang CodeGen of an AArch64-specific source attribute and fixed/scalable SVE vector conversions. They do not exercise InstCombine, Attributor, or LLVM verifier rejection of incompatible attributes.
Pass or subsystem link: Clang AArch64 CodeGen ABI lowering; Clang Itanium name mangling
Causal explanation: This candidate introduces an attribute, but it is a frontend AArch64 type attribute rather than an LLVM IR function/call attribute inferred or rewritten by Attributor. The retrieved hunks have no Attributor, InstCombine attribute propagation, or Verifier changes. The InstCombine ElementCount hunks shown at first-parent distance 5 are context only and must not be attributed to this commit. Type-lowering changes could generally affect generated IR, but the available evidence does not connect them to the issue's incompatible-attribute verifier failure.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Adds target-specific AArch64/SVE ABI and mangling behavior, with assertions requiring expected SVE vector kinds and builtin element types.; Regression coverage is AArch64-target-gated and tests multiple vector widths, casts, globals, and mangling output.; No retrieved test invokes Attributor, InstCombine, or the LLVM verifier on attribute-bearing IR.

Summary: The candidate adds AArch64 support for fixed-length SVE types created with the arm_sve_vector_bits attribute. It introduces ABI coercion from fixed-length SVE data and predicate vectors to corresponding scalable LLVM vector types, adds Itanium mangling for fixed-length SVE vector types, and adds AArch64 CodeGen and mangling tests covering casts, globals, and multiple SVE vector lengths.
Changed symbols: AArch64ABIInfo::coerceIllegalVector; CXXNameMangler::mangleAArch64FixedSveVectorType(const VectorType *); CXXNameMangler::mangleAArch64FixedSveVectorType(const DependentVectorType *)

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This FunctionAttrs refactoring changes addReadAttrs to accumulate obsolete function memory-access attributes in an AttrBuilder and remove them in one Function::removeAttributes call, instead of invoking removeFnAttr once for each attribute. Summary: This commit changes clang-format's TokenAnnotator pointer-declaration parsing so that the nullability tokens _Nonnull, _Nullable, and _Null_unspecified are accepted alongside const, restrict, volatile, and __attribute__ when determining whether a following token acts as a pointer qualifier.
Changed symbols: clang::format::TokenAnnotator
Behavioral change: Treats _Nonnull, _Nullable, and _Null_unspecified as valid tokens following a pointer/reference declarator in the relevant TokenAnnotator lookahead.
Reproducer link: The retrieved change concerns clang-format parsing of source-level nullability spelling, not optimized LLVM IR or verifier rejection.
Pass or subsystem link: clang-format TokenAnnotator

The edits also make FileCheck matching less dependent on a fixed attribute-group numbering/order.

Summary: The candidate changes clang-format token annotation so tok::kw___attribute is accepted by the same pointer-qualifier classification path as the existing qualifier tokens, and adds formatting tests for pointer declarations containing both __attribute__((foo)) and __attribute((foo)).
Changed symbols: clang::format::TokenAnnotator; tok::kw___attribute; FormatTest.UnderstandsUsesOfStarAndAmp; verifyIndependentOfContext
Behavioral change: Treats __attribute as a pointer qualifier in clang-format's token annotation logic.; Adds unit coverage that formatting is stable both at top level and inside a function for attribute-decorated pointer declarations.; This changes source-format parsing/classification, not LLVM IR attribute inference, call-site rewriting, or verifier legality rules.
Assertion or trace link: attribute is a lexical source-token match only; No visible match for Wrong types for attribute, Broken function found, InstCombine, or Attributor
Reproducer link: The new reproducer is clang-format input such as MACRO(A *__attribute__((foo)) a);.; It does not optimize IR or reproduce verifier rejection of incompatible LLVM attributes.
Pass or subsystem link: clang-format; TokenAnnotator

diff --git a/llvm/test/tools/llvm-readobj/ELF/file-header-format.test b/llvm/test/tools/llvm-readobj/ELF/file-header-format.test
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..0a208777fd88
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/tools/llvm-readobj/ELF/file-header-format.test
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+## This tests "Format" values printed by llvm-readobj.
+
+## The "Format" value printed depends on values stored in e_ident[EI_CLASS],
+## e_ident[EI_DATA] and e_machine fields of an ELF file header.
+## We test all possible values in unittests\Object\ELFObjectFileTest.cpp,
+## here we test just a few of them to demonstrate that llvm-readobj prints the same.
+
+# RUN: yaml2obj %s -o %t.none64.o
+# RUN: llvm-readobj --file-headers %t.none64.o | FileCheck %s -DFMT="elf64-unknown"
+
+# RUN: yaml2obj %s -o %t.none32.o -DCLASS=32
+# RUN: llvm-readobj --file-headers %t.none32.o | FileCheck %s -DFMT="elf32-unknown"
+
+# RUN: yaml2obj %s -o %t.i386-32.o -DMACHINE=EM_386 -DCLASS=32
+# RUN: llvm-readobj --file-headers %t.i386-32.o | FileCheck %s -DFMT="elf32-i386"
+
+# RUN: yaml2obj %s -o %t.x86_64.o -DMACHINE=EM_X86_64
+# RUN: llvm-readobj --file-headers %t.x86_64.o | FileCheck %s -DFMT="elf64-x86-64"
+
+# CHECK: Format: [[FMT]]
+
+--- !ELF
+FileHeader:
+  Class:   ELFCLASS[[CLASS=64]]
+  Data:    ELFDATA2[[DATA=LSB]]
+  Type:    ET_REL
+  Machine: [[MACHINE=EM_NONE]]
